## Objective 
This is to parse pathology report info into categories using GPT4o via Microsoft Azure API / Batch processing. 
I use pathology reports from two different archives vmacs, and labl. These are processed with different prompts,
and validated and tested separetly with the outputs combined to one table.

## Deviations
The python scripts used for interaction with microsoft Azure are under fe_si_platforms/azure/scripts/ but the output is under outputs in this repo (subfolders named after script and set)


## Libraries, directories and functions
```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

library(jsonlite)
library(tidyverse)
library(writexl)
library(readxl)
library(forcats)
library(lubridate)
library(eulerr) #for diagram
library(RColorBrewer)
library(cowplot)     # get_legend() and plot_grid()
library(grid)        # unit()
library(scales)
library(glue)

# Function to check if the JSON content follows the expected format
is_correct_format <- function(content, expected_variables) {
  # Try to parse the content as JSON
  parsed <- tryCatch(fromJSON(content), error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # Check if the parsed object contains the required fields
  if (!is.null(parsed) &&
      all(expected_variables %in% names(parsed))) {
    return(TRUE)
  }
  
  return(FALSE)
}

#functions for extracting infp from azure batch output
`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

strip_code_fences <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  if (startsWith(x, "```")) {
    # remove leading ``` or ```json and trailing ```
    x <- sub("^```[a-zA-Z]*\\s*", "", x)
    x <- sub("\\s*```\\s*$", "", x)
  }
  x
}

extract_json_object <- function(x) {
  # robustly grab the first {...} block even if extra text remains
  sub("(?s).*?(\\{.*\\}).*", "\\1", x, perl = TRUE)
}

extract_assistant_text <- function(ch0) {
  cfield <- ch0$message$content
  if (is.list(cfield)) {
    txts <- vapply(cfield, function(p) p$text %||% "", character(1))
    paste(txts[nzchar(txts)], collapse = "\n")
  } else {
    as.character(cfield %||% "")
  }
}

#for calculating performance metrics where some values may be missing
safe_div <- function(num, den) ifelse(den == 0, NA_real_, num / den)

# Compute binary counts & metrics given a "positive class" label
bin_metrics <- function(ref, pred, positive_label) {
  # Drop rows where either side is NA
  df <- tibble(ref = ref, pred = pred) %>% filter(!is.na(ref), !is.na(pred))

  tp <- sum(ref == positive_label & pred == positive_label)
  tn <- sum(ref != positive_label & pred != positive_label)
  fp <- sum(ref != positive_label & pred == positive_label)
  fn <- sum(ref == positive_label & pred != positive_label)
  n  <- tp + tn + fp + fn

  tibble(
    tp = tp, tn = tn, fp = fp, fn = fn, n = n,
    prevalence = safe_div(tp + fn, n),
    se = safe_div(tp, tp + fn),
    sp = safe_div(tn, tn + fp),
    ppv = safe_div(tp, tp + fp),
    npv = safe_div(tn, tn + fn),
    accuracy = safe_div(tp + tn, n),
    f1 = safe_div(2 * tp, 2 * tp + fp + fn)
  )
}

# Given a base variable name (e.g., `si_segment`), return all class labels to evaluate.
# Binary variables are treated as "TRUE" only.
find_classes <- function(data, var) {
  ref_col <- paste0(var, "_ref")
  pred_col <- var
  ref_vals <- data[[ref_col]]
  pred_vals <- data[[pred_col]]

  # logical/binary?
  is_binary <- is.logical(ref_vals) || setequal(na.omit(unique(ref_vals)), c(FALSE, TRUE))
  if (is_binary) return(c(TRUE))

  # Otherwise: multi-class – collect levels from ref and pred, drop NAs
  sort(unique(na.omit(c(as.character(ref_vals), as.character(pred_vals)))))
}

# Is variable multi-class (>2 unique non-NA values in reference)?
is_multiclass <- function(data, var) {
  ref_col <- paste0(var, "_ref")
  n_distinct(na.omit(data[[ref_col]])) > 2
}


# recursively check all character columns
is_utf8 <- function(x) {
  if (is.character(x)) {
    all(validUTF8(x))
  } else if (is.list(x)) {
    all(map_lgl(x, is_utf8))
  } else TRUE
}

# small helper to coerce various date formats to Date
coerce_to_date <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "Date")) return(x)
  if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) return(as.Date(x))
  # Excel serials often sneak in as numeric
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(as.Date(x, origin = "1899-12-30"))
  # Character fallback; adjust format if needed
  suppressWarnings(as.Date(x))
}
```

### Run the gross parsing on the test set via azures batch processing
1. Print the test set for the gross parsing as json here (chunk below)
2. Then parse that to jsonl format for batch processing with gpt4o-mini with the script parse_batch_input_llm_gross.py (version of fe_si_platforms/azure_open_ai/parse_batch_input.py)
3. Then upload it to batch processing on <https://ai.azure.com/resource/batchjobs/>
4. Then download the output file and parse it here (chunk below)

### Parse the gross output from batch processing:
```{r}

batch_data <- readLines("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/gpt_4o_mini_batch/test_gross_gpt4o_mini_batch_output_file-e2d81ed8-daa9-4d58-906b-b3580d153c51.jsonl")

expected_variables <- c("image_name", "bx_id", "bx_slide", "si_segment", "bx_type")

batch_output <- lapply(batch_data, function(item_json) {
  # 1) parse the line into a list
  item <- tryCatch(fromJSON(item_json, simplifyVector = FALSE),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(item)) {
    return(c(parse_error = "TRUE"))
  }

  # 2) safe accessors for common fields
  custom_id <- item$custom_id %||% NA_character_
  ch0 <- tryCatch(item$response$body$choices[[1]], error = function(e) NULL)

  finish_reason <- ch0$finish_reason %||% NA_character_
  # Treat Azure/OpenAI content filter as triggered only if finish_reason=="content_filter"
  content_filter_triggered <- identical(finish_reason, "content_filter")

  # 3) get assistant message text (often JSON you want to parse)
  content_text <- extract_assistant_text(ch0)

  # 4) parse the assistant JSON payload (your expected key/value fields)
  payload <- tryCatch(fromJSON(content_text), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (!is.null(payload)) {
    # Map to expected variables
    extracted_values <- setNames(
      as.character(payload[expected_variables] %||% NA),
      expected_variables
    )
    correct_format <- all(!is.na(extracted_values))
  } else {
    extracted_values <- setNames(
      rep("json_formatting_error", length(expected_variables)),
      expected_variables
    )
    correct_format <- FALSE
  }


  combined <- c(
    custom_id = as.character(custom_id),
    content_filter_triggered = as.character(content_filter_triggered),
    correct_json_format = as.character(correct_format),
    extracted_values
  )
  as.character(combined)
})
    
parsed_batch_output <- do.call(rbind, lapply(batch_output, function(x) as.data.frame(t(x), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  
# Rename the columns 
colnames(parsed_batch_output) <- c("custom_id", "content_filter_triggered", "correct_json_format", 
                            expected_variables)

write_json(parsed_batch_output, "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/parsed_test_gross_gpt4o_mini_batch_output.json")
```
### Calculate performance - gross test
The test sets pulled in the previous chunks were reviewed manually by jmw prior to prompt engineering below.
This chunk is to parse the manually reviewed df to match the output format of the llms
```{r}
test_vmacs <- read_xlsx("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/input/pmi_pilot_data_extract_75.xlsx") %>%
  mutate(si_segment_ref = ifelse(si_section == "si_unspecified", "unspecified", si_section),
         bx_type_ref = ifelse(bx_type == "endoscopic_pinch", "endoscopic", bx_type)) %>%
  select(bx_id, bx_slide, si_segment_ref, bx_type_ref)

parsed_batch_output <- fromJSON("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/parsed_test_gross_gpt4o_mini_batch_output.json") %>%
  select(image_name, bx_id, bx_slide, si_segment, bx_type)

merged_gross <- merge(parsed_batch_output, test_vmacs) %>%
  mutate(correct_segment = ifelse(si_segment == si_segment_ref, TRUE, FALSE),
         correct_type = ifelse(bx_type == bx_type_ref, TRUE, FALSE))

all <- nrow(merged_gross)
true_segment <- sum(merged_gross$correct_segment, na.rm = TRUE)
accuracy_segment <- true_segment/all

true_type <- sum(merged_gross$correct_type, na.rm = TRUE)
accuracy_type <- true_type/all

print(paste0("Accuracy for segment id is: ", accuracy_segment))
print(paste0("Accuracy for biopsy type is: ", accuracy_type))

```

### Prompt engineering and model selection - vmacs_description
Tried extracting si_segment and bx_type from description instead. For this the results were largely concordant with the exception of not being able to differentiate between resections and full thickness in description (both are labelled full thickness). And in one record (na for bx type from both models in the gross fields - GPT4o correctly classified the record as endoscopic pinch while gpt4o mini gave na). For simplicity I will stick with extracting this data from the gross field and use gpt4o mini

### Prompt engineering and model selection - vmacs_dx

### Parse bx_gross and dx in one prompt
Refined strategy primarily based on performance of gross approach in full test set:
The performance of extracting bx_type was subpar (<0.6) whereas extacting bx_segment was suboptimal (<0.9).
Since bx_type is not essential for the paper I am skipping it.
Since si_segment is essential for extracting the right diagnosis for each slide, I refined the prompt to give the llm
access to the full report (not just gross) when assigning. To avoid needing to feed the full report in multiple runs I combined the prompts for si_segment extraction and bx_dx extraction (prompt_gross_and_dx_2.txt).
Prepared new input with all relevant fields here & run compare_models.
GPT4o worked well in the 5 tuning slides - but not GPT4o mini. 
Next printed an input file with the relevant fields to run a test batch on the test set

### Parse the gross_dx output from batch processing:
```{r}

batch_data <- readLines("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/gpt4o_batch/test_gross_dx_file-852cda35-7baf-4b25-bd46-08c631597fee.jsonl")

expected_variables <- c("image_name", 
                        "bx_id", 
                        "bx_slide", 
                        "si_segment", 
                        "bx_dx", 
                        "enteritis_lymphocytic", 
                        "enteritis_other",
                        "lymphoma",
                        "neoplasia_other",
                        "dx_other",
                        "normal",
                        "enteritis_grade",
                        "lymphoma_immunophenotype",
                        "lymphoma_cell_size",
                        "lymphoma_epitheliotropism",
                        "ihc",
                        "clonality")

batch_output <- lapply(batch_data, function(item_json) {
  # 1) parse the line into a list
  item <- tryCatch(fromJSON(item_json, simplifyVector = FALSE),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(item)) {
    return(c(parse_error = "TRUE"))
  }

  # 2) safe accessors for common fields
  custom_id <- item$custom_id %||% NA_character_
  ch0 <- tryCatch(item$response$body$choices[[1]], error = function(e) NULL)

  finish_reason <- ch0$finish_reason %||% NA_character_
  # Treat Azure/OpenAI content filter as triggered only if finish_reason=="content_filter"
  content_filter_triggered <- identical(finish_reason, "content_filter")

  # 3) get assistant message text (often JSON you want to parse)
  content_text <- extract_assistant_text(ch0)
  content_text <- strip_code_fences(content_text)
  content_text <- extract_json_object(content_text)

  # 4) parse the assistant JSON payload (your expected key/value fields)
  payload <- tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON(content_text), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (!is.null(payload)) {
    # Map to expected variables
    extracted_values <- setNames(
      as.character(payload[expected_variables] %||% NA),
      expected_variables
    )
    correct_format <- all(!is.na(extracted_values))
  } else {
    extracted_values <- setNames(
      rep("json_formatting_error", length(expected_variables)),
      expected_variables
    )
    correct_format <- FALSE
  }


  combined <- c(
    custom_id = as.character(custom_id),
    content_filter_triggered = as.character(content_filter_triggered),
    correct_json_format = as.character(correct_format),
    extracted_values
  )
  as.character(combined)
})

```

### Calculate performance of llm parsing in test set
This chunk is to calculate the classification performance for each variable and class separately.
#### Issues / Deviations
- The reference standard was parsed prior to finalizing the parsing strategy. Worked around by adjusting the ref format below. 
- The llm prompt does not specify how to handle grade ranges (e.g., mild to moderate) - for the ref standard I used the higher level of the range, llm answers modified post-processing to match.
- The llm is prompted to group lymphocytic enteritis and lymphoplasmacytic enteritis as enteritis_lymphocytic, and all other enteritises as enteritis_other. A prominent reference/llm output discrepancis are mixed enteritis including other cells then lymphocytes and plasma cells. The llm typically classify this as both enteritis_lymphocytic and enteritis_other whereas the reference standard has them as enteritis_other. For this project I don't want them as enteritis_lymphocytic but instead of reprompting I will set double positives as enteritis_other only post processing.
- The llm sometimes contradictively assigned an immunophenotype or epitheliotropism to cases not parsed as lymphoma or an enteritis grade to cases without enteritis. This can be handles in post-processing by setting non-enteritises as grade na etc. 
- The field "clonality" is sometimes parsed as TRUE by the llm when clonality is suggested but not performed, can be corrected postprocessing by changing "true" clonalities that are not in the labl archive (this will produce FNs in cases where the clonality was performed elsewhere - comparatively rare)
- The field IHC sometimes gives FP for other ihcs or if IHC was suggested and not done. No simple post-processing solution

```{r}
parsed_batch_output <- fromJSON("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/parsed_test_gross_dx_gpt4o_batch_output.json")

                                           dx == "le" ~ TRUE,
                                           dx == "lpe_lymphoma" ~ TRUE,
                                           TRUE ~ FALSE),
         enteritis_other_ref = case_when(dx == "necrotizing_enteritis" ~ TRUE,
                                     dx == "ee" ~ TRUE,
                                     dx == "me" ~ TRUE,
                                     dx == "me_lymphoma" ~ TRUE,
                                     dx == "lymphoma_me" ~ TRUE,
                                     dx == "ne" ~ TRUE,
                                     TRUE ~ FALSE),
         lymphoma_ref = case_when(dx == "lymphoma" ~ TRUE,
                              dx == "lymphoma_me" ~ TRUE,
                              dx == "lymphoma_other" ~ TRUE,
                              dx == "lpe_lymphoma" ~ TRUE,
                              dx == "me_lymphoma" ~ TRUE,
                              TRUE ~ FALSE),
         neoplasia_other_ref = case_when(dx == "mct" ~ TRUE,
                                     dx == "plasmacytoma" ~ TRUE,
                                     dx == "adenocarcinoma" ~ TRUE,
                                     TRUE ~ FALSE),
         dx_other_ref = case_when(dx == "fibrosis" ~ TRUE,
                              dx == "other" ~ TRUE,
                              TRUE ~ FALSE),
         normal_ref = case_when(dx == "normal" ~ TRUE,
                            TRUE ~ FALSE),
         enteritis_grade_ref = enteritis_grade,
         lymphoma_immunophenotype_ref = case_when(lymphoma_type == "tcl" ~ "t",
                                                  lymphoma_type == "bcl_tcl" ~ "b__t",
                                                  lymphoma_type == "na" ~ "na",
                                                  TRUE ~ NA),
         lymphoma_cell_size_ref = case_when(lymphoma_size == "na" ~ "na",
                                        lymphoma_size == "small" ~ "small",
                                        lymphoma_size == "intermediate" ~ "intermediate",
                                        lymphoma_size == "large" ~ "large",
                                        lymphoma_size == "large_small" ~ "small__large",
                                        TRUE ~ NA), 
         lymphoma_epitheliotropism_ref = case_when(lymphoma_ref == "FALSE" ~ "na",
                                                   (lymphoma_ref == "TRUE" & lymphoma_epitheliotropism == "na") ~ "FALSE",
                                                   TRUE ~ lymphoma_epitheliotropism),
         ihc_ref = ihc,
         clonality_ref = clonality) %>%
  select(bx_id:bx_slide, dx, si_segment_ref:clonality_ref)
         
         
         
         
merged <- merge(parsed_batch_output, test_vmacs) %>%
  rename(bx_dx_ref = dx) %>%
  mutate(enteritis_grade = case_when(enteritis_grade == "mild__moderate" ~ "moderate",

         lymphoma_epitheliotropism = ifelse(lymphoma == FALSE, "na", lymphoma_epitheliotropism)) %>%
  select(image_name, bx_id, bx_slide,si_segment, si_segment_ref, bx_dx, bx_dx_ref, enteritis_lymphocytic, enteritis_lymphocytic_ref, enteritis_other, enteritis_other_ref, lymphoma, lymphoma_ref, neoplasia_other, neoplasia_other_ref, dx_other, dx_other_ref, normal, normal_ref, enteritis_grade, enteritis_grade_ref, lymphoma_immunophenotype,  lymphoma_immunophenotype_ref,lymphoma_cell_size, lymphoma_cell_size_ref, lymphoma_epitheliotropism, lymphoma_epitheliotropism_ref, ihc, ihc_ref, clonality, clonality_ref) 

vars <- c(
  "si_segment",                 # multiclass
  "enteritis_lymphocytic",      # binary
  "enteritis_other",            # binary
  "lymphoma",                   # binary
  "neoplasia_other",            # binary
  "dx_other",                   # binary

### Parse batch output llm gross_dx test
```{r}
batch_data <- readLines("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/gpt4o_batch/labl_test_file-2d92704d-035a-442a-9e37-3d64021417cd.jsonl")

expected_variables <- c("image_name", 
                        "bx_id", 
                        "bx_slide", 
                        "match",
                        "si_segment", 
                        "bx_dx", 
                        "enteritis_lymphocytic", 
                        "enteritis_other",
                        "lymphoma",
                        "neoplasia_other",
                        "dx_other",
                        "normal",
                        "enteritis_grade",
                        "lymphoma_immunophenotype",
                        "lymphoma_cell_size",
                        "lymphoma_epitheliotropism",
                        "ihc",
                        "clonality")

batch_output <- lapply(batch_data, function(item_json) {
  # 1) parse the line into a list
  item <- tryCatch(fromJSON(item_json, simplifyVector = FALSE),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(item)) {
    return(c(parse_error = "TRUE"))
  }

  # 2) safe accessors for common fields
  custom_id <- item$custom_id %||% NA_character_
  ch0 <- tryCatch(item$response$body$choices[[1]], error = function(e) NULL)

  finish_reason <- ch0$finish_reason %||% NA_character_
  # Treat Azure/OpenAI content filter as triggered only if finish_reason=="content_filter"
  content_filter_triggered <- identical(finish_reason, "content_filter")

  # 3) get assistant message text (often JSON you want to parse)
  content_text <- extract_assistant_text(ch0)
  content_text <- strip_code_fences(content_text)
  content_text <- extract_json_object(content_text)

  # 4) parse the assistant JSON payload (your expected key/value fields)
  payload <- tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON(content_text), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (!is.null(payload)) {
    # Map to expected variables
    extracted_values <- setNames(
      as.character(payload[expected_variables] %||% NA),
      expected_variables
    )
    correct_format <- all(!is.na(extracted_values))
  } else {
    extracted_values <- setNames(
      rep("json_formatting_error", length(expected_variables)),
      expected_variables
    )
    correct_format <- FALSE
  }


  combined <- c(
    custom_id = as.character(custom_id),
    content_filter_triggered = as.character(content_filter_triggered),
    correct_json_format = as.character(correct_format),
    extracted_values
  )
  as.character(combined)
})
    
parsed_batch_output <- do.call(rbind, lapply(batch_output, function(x) as.data.frame(t(x), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  
# Rename the columns 
colnames(parsed_batch_output) <- c("custom_id", "content_filter_triggered", "correct_json_format", 
                            expected_variables)

write_json(parsed_batch_output, "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/parsed_labl_test_gpt4o_batch_output.json")

```

### Performance labl test
Compared manually parsed info for test set (by jmw) -  saved in input (labl_pilot_data_extract_75_2025-10-31)
Ran test set with GPT4o using selected prompt (see above) (input/parse_path_report/prompt_gross_and_dx_labl_3) using azure batch (input parsed with scripts/parse_batch_input_llm_gross_dx)
Overall this worked well with discrepancies listed below:
#### Issues
##### Serious - consider not using
- ihc - the llm consistently overcalled that ihc had been done with little/no evidence thereof - this info could not reliably be used
##### Minor / solvable
- "si_segment": Blocks named "D" often interpteted as duodenum  by llm if not other si_segment specified 
- "dx_other": The llm sometimes erroneously included clonality results as additional diagnosis
- "normal": The llm consistently labelled reports with missing information as normal - too far of a stretch for this archive
- lymphoma_immunophenotype and lymphoma_epitheliotropism; The llm consistenly labelled records not classified as lymphoma as t and/or epitheliotropic if these were mentioned - could be solved post-processing
##### Minor - acceptable interpretaions - could be used as is
- "match" : When uncertain if a match - the llm leaned towards false while human true (acceptable error)
- "enteritis-grade" the llm consistently used the grade for epithelotropism as the grade for enteritis - acceptable

## Compiled Local & External
### Performance (compiled & cleaned for pub)
```{r}
local <- read_xlsx("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/input/parse_path_report/llm_metrics_commented.xlsx") %>%
  filter(variable__class != "si_segment__jejunum__ileum") %>% # only one instance (correctly parsed) - remove for simplicity 
  filter(variable__class != "si_segment__unspecified") %>%  # errors already reflected in duo/jej/ileum classes 
  filter(variable__class != "enteritis_grade__na") %>% #errors already reflected in other classes
  filter(variable__class != "lymphoma_cell_size__na") %>% #errors already reflected in other classes
  filter(variable__class != "lymphoma_immunophenotype__na") %>% #errors already reflected in other classes
  filter(variable__class != "lymphoma_epitheliotropism__FALSE") %>% #errors already reflected in other classes
  filter(variable__class != "lymphoma_epitheliotropism__na") %>% #errors already reflected in other classes
   mutate(
    class = if_else(class == "b__t", "b", class),
    variable__class = if_else(variable__class == "lymphoma_immunophenotype__b__t",
                              "lymphoma_immunophenotype__b",
                              variable__class) #only one instance with both a b and t cell lymphoma - simplify to b
  )

#combine minimal and mild (low prev of minimal - only error is minimal/mild confusion -> inconsequential)
to_merge <- c("enteritis_grade__minimal", "enteritis_grade__mild")
rows <- local %>% 
  filter(variable__class %in% to_merge)

n_new  <- sum(rows$n,  na.rm = TRUE) /2
tp_new <- sum(rows$tp + rows$fp, na.rm = TRUE)   # TP = TP+FP from both classes
fp_new <- 0L
fn_new <- 0L
tn_new <- n_new - tp_new

new_row <- tibble(
  variable        = "enteritis_grade",
  class           = "mild",
  variable__class = "enteritis__grade_mild",
  tp = tp_new,
  tn = tn_new,
  fp = fp_new,
  fn = fn_new,
  n  = n_new
) %>%
  mutate(
    prevalence = ifelse(n > 0, (tp + fn) / n, NA_real_),
    se         = ifelse((tp + fn) > 0, tp / (tp + fn), NA_real_),
    sp         = ifelse((tn + fp) > 0, tn / (tn + fp), NA_real_),
    ppv        = ifelse((tp + fp) > 0, tp / (tp + fp), NA_real_),
    npv        = ifelse((tn + fn) > 0, tn / (tn + fn), NA_real_),
    accuracy   = ifelse(n > 0, (tp + tn) / n, NA_real_),
    f1         = ifelse((2 * tp + fp + fn) > 0, 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn), NA_real_),
    comment_errors = "Minimal merged into mild; within-class confusions collapse to TP"
  )

local_merged <- local %>%
  filter(!variable__class %in% to_merge) %>%
  bind_rows(new_row)

#combined marked and severe - because few cases (no confusion amongst them)

to_merge2 <- c("enteritis_grade__marked", "enteritis_grade__severe")

rows2 <- local_merged %>%
  filter(variable__class %in% to_merge2)

# extract existing comment from the 'marked' row (if any)
comment_marked <- rows2 %>%
  filter(variable__class == "enteritis_grade__marked") %>%
  pull(comment_errors) %>%
  paste(collapse = "; ")

# apply your rules
n_new2  <- sum(rows2$n,  na.rm = TRUE) / 2
tp_new2 <- sum(rows2$tp, na.rm = TRUE)
fp_new2 <- sum(rows2$fp, na.rm = TRUE)
fn_new2 <- sum(rows2$fn, na.rm = TRUE)
tn_new2 <- n_new2 - (tp_new2 + fp_new2 + fn_new2)

# construct the new merged row
new_row2 <- tibble(
  variable        = "enteritis_grade",
  class           = "marked",
  variable__class = "enteritis__grade_marked",
  tp = tp_new2,
  tn = tn_new2,
  fp = fp_new2,
  fn = fn_new2,
  n  = n_new2
) %>%
  mutate(
    prevalence = ifelse(n > 0, (tp + fn) / n, NA_real_),
    se         = ifelse((tp + fn) > 0, tp / (tp + fn), NA_real_),
    sp         = ifelse((tn + fp) > 0, tn / (tn + fp), NA_real_),
    ppv        = ifelse((tp + fp) > 0, tp / (tp + fp), NA_real_),
    npv        = ifelse((tn + fn) > 0, tn / (tn + fn), NA_real_),
    accuracy   = ifelse(n > 0, (tp + tn) / n, NA_real_),
    f1         = ifelse((2 * tp + fp + fn) > 0, 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn), NA_real_),
    comment_errors = paste(
      "Marked and severe merged by summing TP/FP/FN; n = sum(n)/2; TN = n - (TP+FP+FN).",
      comment_marked
    )
  )

# replace old rows with the merged one
local_merged2 <- local_merged %>%
  filter(!variable__class %in% to_merge2) %>%
  bind_rows(new_row2)

## Analysis, parse, clean and combine
### Parse all local vmacs - batch output
```{r}
batch_data <- readLines("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/gpt4o_batch/all_gross_dx_gpt4o_file-19cba428-769d-4bd9-9ae6-a91801457dde.jsonl")

expected_variables <- c("image_name", 
                        "bx_id", 
                        "bx_slide", 
                        "si_segment", 
                        "bx_dx", 
                        "enteritis_lymphocytic", 
                        "enteritis_other",
                        "lymphoma",
                        "neoplasia_other",
                        "dx_other",
                        "normal",
                        "enteritis_grade",
                        "lymphoma_immunophenotype",
                        "lymphoma_cell_size",
                        "lymphoma_epitheliotropism",
                        "ihc",
                        "clonality")

batch_output <- lapply(batch_data, function(item_json) {
  # 1) parse the line into a list
  item <- tryCatch(fromJSON(item_json, simplifyVector = FALSE),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(item)) {
    return(c(parse_error = "TRUE"))
  }

  # 2) safe accessors for common fields
  custom_id <- item$custom_id %||% NA_character_
  ch0 <- tryCatch(item$response$body$choices[[1]], error = function(e) NULL)

  finish_reason <- ch0$finish_reason %||% NA_character_
  # Treat Azure/OpenAI content filter as triggered only if finish_reason=="content_filter"
  content_filter_triggered <- identical(finish_reason, "content_filter")

  # 3) get assistant message text (often JSON you want to parse)
  content_text <- extract_assistant_text(ch0)
  content_text <- strip_code_fences(content_text)
  content_text <- extract_json_object(content_text)

  # 4) parse the assistant JSON payload (your expected key/value fields)
  payload <- tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON(content_text), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (!is.null(payload)) {
    # Map to expected variables
    extracted_values <- setNames(
      as.character(payload[expected_variables] %||% NA),
      expected_variables
    )
    correct_format <- all(!is.na(extracted_values))
  } else {
    extracted_values <- setNames(
      rep("json_formatting_error", length(expected_variables)),
      expected_variables
    )
    correct_format <- FALSE
  }


  combined <- c(
    custom_id = as.character(custom_id),
    content_filter_triggered = as.character(content_filter_triggered),
    correct_json_format = as.character(correct_format),
    extracted_values
  )
  as.character(combined)
})
    
parsed_batch_output <- do.call(rbind, lapply(batch_output, function(x) as.data.frame(t(x), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  
# Rename the columns 
colnames(parsed_batch_output) <- c("custom_id", "content_filter_triggered", "correct_json_format", 
                            expected_variables)

write_json(parsed_batch_output, "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/all_gross_dx_gpt4o_batch_output.json")

dob_tbl <- fromJSON("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/dob_patients.json")

# handle age 
# Infer century for 2-digit years (assumes <= current YY => 2000s, else 1900s)
infer_century <- function(two_digit) {
  y2 <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(two_digit))
  if (is.na(y2)) return(NA_integer_)
  cutoff <- as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%y"))
  if (y2 <= cutoff) 2000L + y2 else 1900L + y2
}

# Extract birth year (YYYY) from a single string
extract_birth_year <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return(NA_integer_)
  s <- tolower(trimws(x))

  # 1) Prefer a 4-digit year inside parentheses (e.g., "8yo (~2020)")
  m <- str_match(s, "\\((?:~\\s*)?(\\d{4})\\)")
  if (!is.na(m[,2])) return(as.integer(m[,2]))

  # 2) Year ranges like "YYYY-YYYY" or "~YYYY-YYYY" -> take the first YYYY
  m <- str_match(s, "~?\\s*(\\d{4})\\s*-\\s*(\\d{4})")
  if (!is.na(m[,2])) return(as.integer(m[,2]))

  # 3) Any standalone 4-digit year (covers YYYY, M/D/YYYY, M/YYYY)
  m <- str_match(s, "(\\d{4})")
  if (!is.na(m[,2])) return(as.integer(m[,2]))

  # 4) Text month with 2-digit year (e.g., "DD/sept/23" or "12/Sept/09")
  #    Capture the last 2-digit token if a month name is present
  if (str_detect(s, "(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|MAY|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Sept|Oct|Nov|Dec)")) {
    m2 <- str_match(s, "(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|MAY|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Sept|Oct|Nov|Dec)[^0-9]*?(\\d{2})(?!\\d)")
    if (!is.na(m2[,2])) return(infer_century(m2[,2]))
  }

  # 5) Nothing found
  NA_integer_
}

# Extract age in years (numeric) from a single string
extract_age_years <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return(NA_real_)
  s <- tolower(trimws(x))

  # NA-like strings
  if (s %in% c("NA", "na", "not specified", "unk")) return(NA_real_)

  # base years: handles "11yo", "5+ years", "7 yrs", "10 year"
  # capture the first integer before "yo", "years", "yrs", "y"
  m_years <- str_match(s, "(\\d+)\\s*\\+?\\s*(?:years?|yrs?|yo|y)\\b")
  yrs <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m_years[,2]))

  # months: handles "7yo11months", "11 months", "11mos"
  m_months <- str_match(s, "(\\d+)\\s*(?:months?|mos?)\\b")
  mos <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m_months[,2]))

  # If string is just something like "11yo" (already caught above) we're good.
  # If it’s only months without years, don’t treat that as a valid age in years.
  if (is.na(yrs) && !is.na(mos)) {
    # if you prefer to convert months-only to years, uncomment:
    # return(round(mos / 12, 2))
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  if (is.na(yrs)) return(NA_real_)
  if (!is.na(mos)) yrs <- yrs + mos / 12
  round(yrs, 2)
}

all_wsis_age_prep <- all_wsis %>%
  mutate(
    birth_year = map_int(labl_dob_age, extract_birth_year),
    labl_age_years  = map_dbl(labl_dob_age, extract_age_years)
  )

to_date <- function(x) {
  # already Date/POSIX/numeric Excel serials
  if (inherits(x, "Date"))   return(x)
  if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) return(as.Date(x))
  if (is.numeric(x))         return(as.Date(x, origin = "1899-12-30"))

  s <- as.character(x)
  # NEW: keep only the part before "|||"
  s <- trimws(sub("\\|\\|\\|.*$", "", s))

  out <- as.Date(NA_real_)

  # try timestamp "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" (and variants)
  tmp <- suppressWarnings(lubridate::ymd_hms(s, tz = "UTC", quiet = TRUE))
  out <- ifelse(!is.na(tmp), as.Date(tmp), out)

  # plain ISO date "YYYY-MM-DD"
  tmp <- suppressWarnings(lubridate::ymd(s, quiet = TRUE))
  out <- ifelse(is.na(out) & !is.na(tmp), as.Date(tmp), out)

  # common alt orders
  tmp <- suppressWarnings(lubridate::mdy(s, quiet = TRUE))
  out <- ifelse(is.na(out) & !is.na(tmp), as.Date(tmp), out)

  tmp <- suppressWarnings(lubridate::dmy(s, quiet = TRUE))
  out <- ifelse(is.na(out) & !is.na(tmp), as.Date(tmp), out)

  # month names / mixed formats
  tmp <- suppressWarnings(lubridate::parse_date_time(
    s,
    orders = c("Ymd HMS","Ymd HM","Ymd H","dbY","dby","bdY","bdy","mdY","dmy"),
    tz = "UTC"
  ))
  out <- ifelse(is.na(out) & !is.na(tmp), as.Date(tmp), out)

  as.Date(out, origin = "1970-01-01")
}

all_wsis_age <- all_wsis_age_prep %>%
  mutate(
    # Coerce inputs
    bx_date   = to_date(vmacs_bx_date),
    dob_date  = to_date(date_of_birth),
    lbl_date  = to_date(labl_date),
    byear_int = suppressWarnings(as.integer(birth_year)),
    labl_age_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(labl_age_years)),

    # 1) From two dates (preferred)
    age_from_dates = if_else(
      !is.na(bx_date) & !is.na(dob_date),
      floor(time_length(interval(dob_date, bx_date), "years")),
      NA_real_
    ),

    # 2) From labl_age_years
    age_from_label = if_else(!is.na(labl_age_num), floor(labl_age_num), NA_real_),

    # 3) From birth_year and labl_date (uses calendar years difference)
    age_from_by_ld = if_else(
      !is.na(byear_int) & !is.na(lbl_date),
      floor(year(lbl_date) - byear_int),
      NA_real_
    ),

    # Priority: dates → label → birth_year + labl_date
    age_years = coalesce(age_from_dates, age_from_label, age_from_by_ld),
    bx_year = coalesce(
      vmacs_bx_year,
      year(to_date(labl_date)))) %>%
  select(-bx_date, -dob_date, -lbl_date, -byear_int, -labl_age_num,
         -age_from_dates, -age_from_label, -age_from_by_ld)

#Handle breed
# --- Canonical mapping (add to this as you encounter more forms) ---
breed_map <- c(
  "DSH" = "DSH",
  "DLH" = "DLH",
  "DMH" = "DMH",
  "DSJ" = "Domestic Short Hair",        # likely typo for DSH
  "AMERICAN DOMESTIC SHORTHAIR" = "Domestic Short Hair",

  "SIAM" = "Siamese",
  "SIAMESE" = "Siamese",
  "ABBY" = "Abyssinian",
  "ABYSSINIAN" = "Abyssinian",
  "AMERICAN SHORTHAIR" = "American Shorthair",
  "EUROPEAN SHORTHAIR" = "European Shorthair",
  "NORWEGIAN FOREST CAT" = "Norwegian Forest Cat",
  "RUSSIAN BLUE" = "Russian Blue",
  "SPHYNX" = "Sphynx",
  "SNOWSHOE" = "Snowshoe",
  "PERSIAN" = "Persian",
  "HIMALAYAN" = "Himalayan",
  "RAGDOLL" = "Ragdoll",
  "BIRMAN" = "Birman",
  "BENGAL" = "Bengal",
  "BENGALESE" = "Bengal",               # seen variant
  "MAINE" = "Maine Coon",
  "MAINE COON" = "Maine Coon",
  "SCOTTISH FOLD" = "Scottish Fold",
  "MANX" = "Manx",
  "BOBTAIL" = "Bobtail",                # generic (could refine to American/Japanese)
  "REX" = "Rex",                        # generic (Cornish/Devon if known)
  "CORNISH REX" = "Cornish Rex",
  "TOYGER" = "Toyger",
  "SAVANNAH" = "Savannah",
  "JUNGLE CAT" = "Jungle Cat",
  "EGY MAU" = "Egyptian Mau",
  "EGYPTIAN MAU" = "Egyptian Mau",
  "TURKISH ANGORA" = "Turkish Angora",
  "SCOTTISH FOLD" = "Scottish Fold",
  "BOMBAY" = "Bombay",

  # labl values you showed explicitly:
  "ABYSSINIAN" = "Abyssinian",
  "MAINE COON MIX" = "Maine Coon",      # will still tag as Mix via rule below
  "CALICO" = "Calico",                  # pattern, but keep as given
  "LYNX"   = "Lynx"                     # often a pattern (lynx point); keep literal
)

unknown_tokens <- c("IR","AIR","TIC","FV","X")  # treat these as non-breeds/unknown

# --- Normalizer for a single cell from either column ---
normalize_breed <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x)) return(NA_character_)

  s <- str_squish(toupper(as.character(x)))

  # trivial missing values
  if (s %in% c("", "NA", "NOT SPECIFIED")) return(NA_character_)

  # Remove FE- prefix
  s <- str_remove(s, "^FE-")

  # Flag mixes
  is_mix <- str_detect(s, "\\bMIX\\b") || str_detect(s, "\\bX/") || str_detect(s, "/")

  # Remove "X/" markers but keep slash-separated components
  s <- str_replace_all(s, "\\bX/", "")

  # Split by "/" into components
  parts <- unlist(str_split(s, "/"))
  parts <- str_squish(parts)
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]

  # Map tokens to canonical names
  canon <- map_chr(parts, function(tok) {
    # direct dictionary hit
    if (tok %in% names(breed_map)) return(breed_map[[tok]])

    # try some common multiword recoveries after general cleanup
    tok2 <- tok %>%
      str_replace_all("-", " ") %>%
      str_squish()

    if (tok2 %in% names(breed_map)) return(breed_map[[tok2]])

    # If token includes words like "MAINE COON", "SCOTTISH FOLD", etc.
    # catch those by searching the map keys that are substrings
    hits <- names(breed_map)[str_detect(tok2, fixed(names(breed_map)))]
    if (length(hits) > 0) return(breed_map[[hits[[1]]]])

    # drop clearly unknown codes
    if (tok %in% unknown_tokens) return(NA_character_)

    # If "MIX" token appears as its own part, drop it (we already set is_mix)
    if (tok == "MIX") return(NA_character_)

    # Otherwise, keep readable token (e.g., already full name like "ABYSSINIAN", "RUSSIAN BLUE")
    str_to_title(tok2)
  })

  canon <- unique(na.omit(canon))
  if (length(canon) == 0) return(NA_character_)

  # If only one breed and string didn't indicate a mix → just that breed
  if (!is_mix && length(canon) == 1) {
    return(canon[1])
  }

  # Otherwise, present as a mix of the mapped breeds
  paste0(paste(canon, collapse = " / "), " Mix")
}

# --- Apply to both columns, prioritize VMACS, then LABL ---
all_wsis_breed <- all_wsis_age %>%
  mutate(
    vmacs_breed_norm = map_chr(vmacs_breed, normalize_breed),
    labl_breed_norm  = map_chr(labl_breed,  normalize_breed),
    breed   = coalesce(vmacs_breed_norm, labl_breed_norm)
  )

Set composition
```{r}
# Fig S1 A set overlap
all_wsis_info_vmacs_labl <- fromJSON("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/all_wsis_parsed_info.json")

# (1) One row per WSI to avoid double-counting
df_sets <- all_wsis_info_vmacs_labl %>%
  distinct(image_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

# (2) Build the member lists for each set (all are logicals)
sets <- with(df_sets, list(
  "Model development"  = image_name[model_development_set],
  "Model test"          = image_name[model_test_set],
  "Pathologist grading"   = image_name[pathologist_grading_set],
  "Feature tuning" = image_name[feature_tuning_set],
  "Analysis"      = image_name[analysis_set]
))

# (3) Fit an area-proportional Euler diagram
fit <- euler(sets)   # eulerr estimates circle/overlap areas from memberships

# (4) Plot: areas and overlaps are proportional; add counts on the diagram
png(

#Helper to combine S1b and S1c
fix_right_legend <- function(
  p,
  legend_title,
  plot_width_in   = 2.7,
  legend_width_in = 0.8,
  height_in       = 3.5,
  legend_key_cm   = 0.3,
  text_size       = 10,
  family          = "Arial"
) {
  leg <- cowplot::get_legend(
    p +
      labs(fill = legend_title) +
      guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
      theme(
        legend.position   = "right",
        legend.title      = element_text(size = text_size, family = family, face = "bold"),
        legend.text       = element_text(size = text_size, family = family),
        legend.key.size   = unit(legend_key_cm, "cm"),
        legend.spacing.y  = unit(0.05, "cm"),
        legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
      )
  )

  p_noleg <- p + theme(legend.position = "none")

  cowplot::plot_grid(
    p_noleg, leg,
    ncol = 2,
    rel_widths = c(plot_width_in, legend_width_in),
    align = "h"
  )
}

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
library(scales)

all_wsis_simplified_dx <- fromJSON("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/all_wsis_simplified_dx.json")

# Desired x-axis order
dx_order <- c("Lymphoma", "LPE", "Other", "Multiple", "Normal")

# Desired legend order for dx_categories
dxcat_levels <- c(
  "SCL", "ICL", "LCL",
  "Mild", "Moderate", "Marked",
  "Enteritis", "Neoplasia", "Other", "Neoplasia & Enteritis",
  "Lymphoma & LPE", "Lymphoma & Other", "LPE & Other",
  "Unspecified", "NA"
)

# Palette for dx_categories (keys must match levels exactly)
pal_dxcat <- c(
  "SCL" = "#fdd0a2", "ICL" = "#fd8d3c", "LCL" = "#99000d",
  "Mild" = "#c6dbef", "Moderate" = "#4292c6", "Marked" =  "#084594",
   "Other" = "#dadaeb", "Neoplasia" = "#9e9ac8",  "Enteritis" = "#6a51a3", "Neoplasia & Enteritis" = "#3f007d",
  "Lymphoma & LPE" = "#662506", "Lymphoma & Other" =  "#fec44f", "LPE & Other" = "#fff7bc",
  "Unspecified" = "#f0f0f0", "NA" = "#a1d99b"
)

# Aggregate counts, enforce factor orders, and keep NA as an explicit level
plot_df <- all_wsis_simplified_dx %>%
  filter(analysis_set) %>%
  mutate(
    simplified_dx = factor(simplified_dx, levels = dx_order),
    dx_categories = fct_explicit_na(dx_categories, na_level = "NA"),
    dx_categories = factor(dx_categories, levels = dxcat_levels)
  ) %>%
  count(simplified_dx, dx_categories, name = "n")

# Stacked percent bars by dx_categories
p_dx_pct <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = simplified_dx, y = n, fill = dx_categories)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = pal_dxcat,
    breaks = dxcat_levels,   # legend order
    drop = FALSE,
    name = "dx_categories"
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Percentage of WSIs", fill = "") +
  theme_bw(base_family = "Arial", base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_dx_pct)

  ggsave(
  "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/dx_pct_analysis_set.png",
  p_dx_pct, width = 7, height = 3.5, units = "in", dpi = 300)

```{r}

ggsave("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/dx_analysis_set.png", p_dx_glide, width = 3.5, height = 3.5, units = "in", dpi = 300)

#Figs 3 panel
# Plot (left) + Legend (right) with fixed *absolute* widths
fix_right_legend <- function(
  p,
  legend_title,
  plot_width_in   = 2,
  legend_width_in = 1.5,
  height_in       = 3.5,
  legend_key_cm   = 0.3,
  text_size       = 10,
  family          = "Arial"
) {
  # Build a consistent, single-column legend with a header
  leg <- cowplot::get_legend(
    p +
      labs(fill = legend_title) +
      guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
      theme(
        legend.position   = "right",
        legend.title      = element_text(size = text_size, family = family, face = "bold"),
        legend.text       = element_text(size = text_size, family = family),
        legend.key.size   = unit(legend_key_cm, "cm"),
        legend.spacing.y  = unit(0.05, "cm"),
        legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
      )
  )

  p_noleg <- p + theme(legend.position = "none")

  # Combine with absolute-ish proportions: 3.5 in plot : 1.5 in legend
  cowplot::plot_grid(
    p_noleg, leg,
    ncol = 2,
    rel_widths = c(plot_width_in, legend_width_in),
    align = "h"
  )
}



p_age_fixed   <- fix_right_legend(p_age_glide,   "Age (years)")
p_breed_fixed <- fix_right_legend(p_breed_glide, "Breed")
p_si_fixed    <- fix_right_legend(p_si_glide,    "Small intestinal segment")
p_dx_fixed    <- fix_right_legend(p_dx_glide,    "Diagnosis")

# Example: save one composite at exactly 5" x 3.5" @ 300 dpi
ggsave("age_with_legend.png", p_age_fixed, width = 5, height = 3.5, units = "in", dpi = 300)

# If you assemble a 2×2 panel of these composites:
panel <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  p_age_fixed, p_breed_fixed,
  p_si_fixed,  p_dx_fixed,
  ncol = 2
)

ggsave("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/unsupervised_clustering_fe_si_bx/output/parse_path_report/analysis_set_panel.png", panel, width = 7, height = 7, units = "in", dpi = 300)
